body:
## Le Creuset prices to aim for this Black Friday

These are the prices worth paying, based on last year's sales and today's prices. If you see a piece at or below this figure, it's a genuinely good deal.

- **Signature round casserole, 24cm:** £200 to £225. It sold for £223 on Amazon (Deep Teal) at Black Friday 2025, and it's £203.03 today in Caribbean.
- **Signature round casserole, 20cm:** under £160.
- **Signature round casserole, 28cm:** under £300.
- **Signature shallow casserole, 26cm:** around £220.
- **Stoneware set of 4 mugs:** about £31 to £35. Le Creuset's own Black Friday sale in 2024 had them at £31.
- **Stoneware rectangular dishes:** Le Creuset cut a single 32cm dish to £29 and a set of two to £60 in its 2024 sale. In 2025 its classic baking dish was £27.30, down from £39.

Full prices for the Signature range have risen. Today the uncut colours sell for about £265 (20cm), £335 (24cm) and £405 (28cm), so a discounted colour can save you £100 or more.

## Which Le Creuset pieces are worth it?

**Start with a round casserole.** This is the piece people use for decades. The **24cm (4.2 litres)** suits most homes of two to four people. It holds a stew, a curry or a pot-roast chicken, and it's the classic size for baking bread. Go for the **20cm** if you mostly cook for one or two, or want a second pot for rice and sides. The **26cm and 28cm** are for big families and batch cooking. Bear in mind that the 28cm is heavy when full, and that matters if you have weak wrists or high cupboards.

**Round or shallow?** A shallow casserole (sometimes called a braiser) has more base area and lower sides. It's better for browning meat, shakshuka, risotto and dishes you finish in the oven. If you already have a round pot, a shallow one is the most useful second piece.

**Signature vs the older Classic range.** Signature is the current range, with bigger handles, a heat-resistant knob and a lighter sand-coloured enamel inside. Classic pieces still turn up in sales, often at bigger discounts. They cook just as well, so they're a fair way to save money.

**Cast iron vs stoneware.** Stoneware (mugs, baking dishes, ramekins, pie dishes) is much cheaper, lighter and goes in the dishwasher, but it can't go on the hob. It makes a better gift if your budget is under £60. Stoneware also gets the deepest Black Friday cuts, often 40% to 50% off on Le Creuset's own site.

## When do Le Creuset prices drop?

Black Friday 2026 is on **Friday 27 November**, and Cyber Monday on **30 November**. In past years, Le Creuset's own website launched its sale in Black Friday week, with the biggest cuts on stoneware and selected cast-iron colours. John Lewis usually matches it on some lines.

Amazon is different: Le Creuset prices there move all year, and individual colours drop at random. That's why the 24cm is already cheaper than last Black Friday. If the size and colour you want hits the target price above, there's little point waiting.

Many of Amazon's Black Friday prices are for Prime members only. If you're not a member, a [Prime free trial](https://www.amazon.co.uk/amazonprime) covers the whole sale period. See our [Amazon Prime free trial guide](/guides/amazon-prime-free-trial-black-friday-2026/) for how to time it.

### Is Le Creuset cheaper on Black Friday?

Usually, yes, but not always on Amazon. Le Creuset's own sale and John Lewis cut prices in Black Friday week, while Amazon prices go up and down by colour all year. Compare today's price with the targets above before you decide.

### What size Le Creuset casserole should I buy?

For most people, the 24cm. It feeds about four and is the size most recipes assume. Pick 20cm for one or two people, and 26cm or 28cm if you regularly cook for six or more.

### Why are some colours much cheaper than others?

Amazon and other retailers discount colours they want to clear, while new or popular shades stay at full price. The pot is identical apart from the enamel colour, so being flexible is the easiest way to save £50 to £100.

### Is Le Creuset worth the money?

If you'll use it every week, yes. Enamelled cast iron holds heat evenly, goes from hob to oven, and comes with a lifetime guarantee on cast iron. If you only make the odd casserole, a cheaper cast-iron pot will do the job.
